={
  "model": "claude-opus-4-8",
  "max_tokens": 2048,
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        {
          "type": "image",
          "source": {
            "type": "base64",
            "media_type": "image/jpeg",
            "data": "{{ $('Trigger Context').item.json.image_base64 }}"
          }
        },
        {
          "type": "text",
          "text": "You are a meticulous financial-document examiner reading a PHOTOGRAPH of a paper check sent by a project manager at a countertop company. Accuracy is critical: this number controls how much money gets recorded. Read slowly and verify every single digit.

ORIENTATION: the photo may be rotated, tilted, or upside down. First mentally rotate it so the text is upright, THEN read.

The PM may have typed a caption naming the customer. PM caption: [{{ ($('Trigger Context').item.json.caption || 'no caption').split('"').join(' ').split('
').join(' ') }}]

FIRST, look at the image and decide what it is. Set document_type to 'cash' if the image shows physical cash or currency bills (NOT a check), 'check' if it is a paper bank check, otherwise 'other'. If it is cash, do NOT read an amount or check number off the image - the PM types those in the caption, so capture them as cash_amount and cash_invoice from the caption instead.

A check states the amount TWICE and the check number TWICE on purpose. Use that redundancy to catch your own mistakes.

AMOUNT - read it two INDEPENDENT ways, then reconcile:
1) The courtesy box (the digits right after the $ sign). Read it digit by digit. These pairs are commonly confused on handwritten/printed checks - look hard: 8 vs 5, 8 vs 6, 8 vs 3, 5 vs 6, 1 vs 7, 0 vs 6, 9 vs 4.
2) The legal line (the amount written out in words). Transcribe the words EXACTLY as written, then convert those words to a number yourself.
The courtesy figure and the legal words MUST resolve to the SAME number. If they disagree, you have misread one of them - go back and re-read both digit by digit until they reconcile. Mark amount_confidence 'high' ONLY when the figures and the words independently give the same number. If they still disagree after careful re-reading, follow banking convention: the WRITTEN legal amount is authoritative - use it and mark amount_confidence 'low'.

CHECK NUMBER - read it two INDEPENDENT ways, then reconcile:
1) The number in the top-right corner. Read it digit by digit.
2) The MICR line (the blocky magnetic-ink digits along the very bottom). Transcribe the ENTIRE MICR line. The check number is normally the LAST group of digits in it. The MICR line is machine-printed and is the most reliable source - trust it over the corner if they differ.
Mark check_number_confidence 'high' ONLY when the corner and the MICR check number agree.

JOINT PAYERS: a check can be printed with TWO payers (often a married couple) who usually share one surname. When two names are printed, set last_name to that shared surname, set first_name to either person first name, and put BOTH full names into all_payer_names. For a single payer, all_payer_names has one entry.

Respond with ONLY a JSON object. No markdown fences, no text before or after it. Use exactly this shape:

{
  "check_number_corner": "corner number digit by digit e.g. 8-6-6-6, or null",
  "micr_line_raw": "the entire MICR line as you read it",
  "check_number_micr": "check number isolated from the MICR line, digits only, or null",
  "check_number": "your FINAL reconciled check number, digits only",
  "check_number_confidence": "high or low",
  "payer_name": "full name(s) printed top-left, exactly as printed",
  "all_payer_names": ["every full name printed top-left, as an array; usually one entry, but two for a joint account like a married couple"],
  "first_name": "payer FIRST name only, or null for a business",
  "middle_name": "payer middle name or initial if present, else null",
  "last_name": "payer LAST name only, or null for a business",
  "entity_type": "individual or business",
  "street_number": "house/building number from the payer address, else null",
  "street_name": "street name with suffix like Rd/Ave/Ln, else null",
  "zip": "zip code from the payer address, else null",
  "amount_courtesy_raw": "exactly what is written in the $ box, e.g. 3,810.00",
  "amount_numeric": "the courtesy box as a plain number e.g. 3810.00",
  "amount_legal_words": "the legal line transcribed word for word",
  "amount_written": "the legal line converted to a plain number e.g. 3810.00",
  "amounts_match": true,
  "amount": "your FINAL reconciled amount as a plain number",
  "amount_confidence": "high or low",
  "date": "the date written on the check",
  "caption_name": "the customer/job name the PM means in the caption above, NAME ONLY - strip words like deposit/paid/rem/dep/PIF. Preserve underscores and capitalization. null if no caption name",
  "caption_first_name": "first name from the caption name, else null",
  "caption_last_name": "last name from the caption name, else null",
  "payment_hint": "deposit, remainder, or PIF from the caption (dep=deposit, rem=remainder, PIF or paid in full=PIF), else null",
  "document_type": "check, cash, or other - what the IMAGE shows (see instruction above)",
  "cash_amount": "ONLY when document_type is cash: the dollar amount the PM typed in the caption as a plain number e.g. 500; else null",
  "cash_invoice": "ONLY when document_type is cash: the invoice/QB number the PM typed in the caption as digits e.g. 6484; else null"
}

Rules: NEVER guess a digit. If a character is truly illegible after careful study, use null and set the relevant confidence to 'low'. Read amount_numeric and amount_written INDEPENDENTLY before you compare them. caption_name comes ONLY from the caption text in brackets above, never from the check image."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
